'''Ivars Kalviņš'''  (born 2 June 1947) is a Latvian (and former Soviet Union) chemist who invented the prescription drug [[meldonium]], trade-named Mildronate.<ref name="ИК">[http://inventions.lza.lv/izg.php?id=28 Ivars KALVIŅŠ] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091112103548/http://inventions.lza.lv/izg.php?id=28 |date=12 November 2009 }}. Inventions.lza.lv. Retrieved on 14 May 2016.</ref><ref>[http://www.lza.lv/scientists/KalvinsI.htm Ivars KALVINSH] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160313195854/http://www.lza.lv/scientists/KalvinsI.htm |date=13 March 2016 }}. Lza.lv. Retrieved on 14 May 2016.</ref>

==Biography==
In 1969 Kalviņš graduated from the Faculty of Chemistry, [[University of Latvia]],<ref name="ИК"/> and in 1985 defended a [[habilitation]] at the [[Saint Petersburg State University]]. Since 1986 he works at the Riga Institute of Organic Synthesis, which he headed in 2003–2014. Earlier between 1994 and 2000 he served as President of the Latvian Society of Chemistry.

Kalviņš was involved in the synthesis of several drugs, including meldonium, leakadin, [[neramexane]], and [[belinostat]].<ref>[http://www.kvalitates-konference.lv/lv/konferences-temas/lektori/234-ivars-kalvins Ivars Kalviņš] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160309153057/http://www.kvalitates-konference.lv/lv/konferences-temas/lektori/234-ivars-kalvins |date=9 March 2016 }}. Kvalitates-konference.lv. Retrieved on 14 May 2016.</ref>

== Awards and honors ==

Kalviņš is an Officer of [[Order of the Three Stars]] and since 1994 is a full member of the Latvian Academy of Sciences. He was awarded the State Prize of the [[Latvian SSR]] in 1988 and the Grand Medal of Academy of Sciences of Latvia in 2009.<ref>[http://lr4.lsm.lv/lv/raksts/kakie-lyudi/ivars-kalvinsh-mi-fanatiki-i-etim-vs-skazano.a33669/ Иварс Калвиньш: мы фанатики, и этим всё сказано] // Latvijas Radio 4</ref> He was nominated as a finalist for the [[European Inventor Award]] 2015.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/science/european-inventor-award-can-a-british-inventor-win-in-the-oscars-of-innovation-10306192.html |title=European Inventor Award: Can a British inventor win in the 'Oscars of Innovation'?|work=The Independent |accessdate=10 March 2016}}</ref> As a member of a team of authors he received the "Annual Award in Science 2017" for the development of a new and promising compound E1R ([[methylphenylpiracetam]]) for improving memory and treating epilepsy. The E1R is the first known and published positive allosteric modulator of Sigma 1 receptor that improves memory processes and prevents seizures.<ref>{{cite news|title=Pasniegtas balvas par 2017. gada nozīmīgākajiem zinātnes sasniegumiem Latvijā|url=https://www.diena.lv/raksts/latvija/zinas/foto-pasniegtas-balvas-par-2017.-gada-nozimigakajiem-zinatnes-sasniegumiem-latvija-14191353|publisher=Diena|date=16 February 2018}}</ref>
